Meera Patel: Heads-up — we just saw a 3x p95 spike on shared-gpu-pool-beta starting ~18:05 UTC. Appears correlated with a tenant burst.
Ryan Cho: Which tenant? any request IDs?
Meera Patel: tenant=libra-analytics. Root cause looks like kernel autoswitch went from int8-fast -> fallback fp16 for ~4m. Logs below:
Meera Patel: ```
[2026-06-12T18:05:12Z] kernel_select: chosen=int8_fast (mem=82%)
[2026-06-12T18:05:18Z] kernel_select: fallback=fp16_dense (reason=kv_alloc_fail)
[2026-06-12T18:05:22Z] runtime_batcher: batch_size=64 -> 384 (heuristic_burst)
[2026-06-12T18:06:11Z] kv_cache: eviction=prefix_kv (tenant=libra-analytics)
```
Alice Nguyen: Interesting — batcher jumped because their rate pattern changed (lots of concurrent short chats). Our batching heuristic has that exponential ramp when QPS > 250 for 10s.
Joel Harris: If batch grew to 384 on int8 it would OOM the KV arena and trigger kernel fallback. That matches the kv_alloc_fail reason.
Meera Patel: Yep. I pulled a flamegraph — the long tail was mostly in kernel copy + sync after fp16 fallback.
Mateo Ruiz: Any per-tenant throttles active? Dedicated per-tenant concurrent request limits should've prevented batch bloat.
Ryan Cho: On shared pools we rely on per-tenant concurrency caps + sampling to shape the batcher. Looks like libra-analytics was under a short window where their in-flight count was under the cap but many micro-bursts from many connections led to batcher merging them.
SRE-Bot: Incident created: INC-20260612-5243. Notifying oncall.
Meera Patel: Repro plan: run a load job with many small seq_len ~8 requests at t=150 RPS -> expect batch growth. I can fork their traffic pattern in staging.
Alice Nguyen: Also need to check kernel selection policy — it should prefer safe kernels that avoid KV allocation spikes. We have a bug in the policy comparator where memory headroom calc uses stale free_nvram metric.
Joel Harris: I found the comparator diff: we were reading free_kv_slots from cache timestamp 10s old. Patch idea: always read live for decisions when candidate memory delta > 15%.
Ryan Cho: For short mitigation: lower the max batch size cap for shared-gpu-pool-beta from 512->192 and enable strict per-tenant burst-window shaping for 60s. That should prevent fallback.
Meera Patel: Deployed a conservative override at 18:20 UTC: `max_batch_size=192` on pool-beta and `tenant_burst_window=60s`. Early telemetry shows tail restored to baseline.
Deploy-bot: deploy service override applied to shared-gpu-pool-beta by Meera Patel @ 2026-06-12T18:20:10Z :thumbsup:
Mateo Ruiz: Need a follow-up: add a fast-path in the batcher to detect many small seq_len and cap effective batcher aggregation weight. Right now aggregation weights favor larger batch size to improve perf.
Alice Nguyen: Also add a KV eviction metric to the runtime tracing so we can correlate eviction events to kernel switches automatically.
Ryan Cho: Agreed. Action items: (1) revert conservative cap when safe, (2) patch kernel comparator to use live memory, (3) add batching heuristic tweak for many short seqs, (4) add eviction -> kernel switch alert. Assigning: Joel(2), Mateo(3), Alice(4), Meera(1).
Meera Patel: I'll keep the override for 6 hours and ramp down if stable. Thanks everyone.
Joel Harris: I'll open a PR for comparator patch and add unit tests around live memory reads.
Mateo Ruiz: I'll prototype the aggregation-weight change on staging and run synthetic bursts.
Alice Nguyen: I'll add a KV-eviction metric and a rule that triggers Slack if eviction_rate > 0.5% AND kernel_change_count > 1/min.
Ryan Cho: Postmortem template: note that cause was batching heuristic + stale memory sampling -> KV arena pressure -> kernel fallback -> tail amplification (noisy-tenant amplification).
Meera Patel: Filing brief incident summary in incidents channel after oncall ack.
SRE-Bot: oncall acknowledged by Ryan Cho @ 2026-06-12T18:24:02Z
Meera Patel: TL;DR: mitigated with batch-cap + shaping, patch inbound for kernel selection logic, follow-ups for batcher heuristics and eviction alerts.
Ryan Cho: Nice triage speed. :thumbsup:
Joel Harris: ETA for PR review ~3h.
Mateo Ruiz: I'll have staging results in ~6h.
Alice Nguyen: I'll wire the metric in the morning (PST).
Meera Patel: Closing thread when follow-ups are tracked. Thanks all.
